briefs.headline: St. Louis shut out the Reds 3-0
briefs.summary: Kyle Leahy took the win and Andrew Abbott the loss; Riley O'Brien closed it. Cincinnati got nothing on the board and host the Cardinals again tonight.

briefs.summary: A three-run fifth did it at home. Braxton Ashcraft went to 13-5, Keider Montero took the loss and Mason Montgomery picked up his fifth save.

briefs.headline: Milwaukee put 22 on Seattle without reply
briefs.summary: The Brewers' shutout was the widest margin of a 15-game card. The Cubs and Royals won on walkoffs and San Diego and the Dodgers went to extra innings.

sections.note: Sumo got its own search again and sits out for a fifth straight edition. The Japan Sumo Association's English pages carry nothing dated later than an Aug. 5 museum notice, and the September dates in Tokyo are still available only from ticket resellers and travel sites, which this paper does not cite. The one new thing on the JSA's own page is that September is sold out on every day. The banzuke (rankings) release on Aug. 31 remains the next moment a citable outlet has to print the dates.

coming_in.item: The gun bear season opens Aug. 29 in SELECTED COUNTIES only. The county list is not in the pamphlet's summary table, so no county is named here. Daily 1, possession 2, season limit 2; bag limits vary by county and permit class and are on pamphlet pages 33-39.
coming_in.publication: West Virginia Hunting and Trapping Regulations Summary, July 2026 - June 2027

coming_in.item: The recreational flounder season opens 12:01 a.m. Sept. 1 and closes 11:59 p.m. Sept. 14 in coastal and joint waters, one fish per person per day at a 15-inch minimum, hook and line and gig only. Every fish kept must be reported to the division.

prime.item: Coastal waters: 18-inch minimum and 27-inch maximum total length, one per day. It is unlawful to possess a red drum over 27 inches or to gig, spear or gaff one.
Coastal waters: 14 to 20 inches total length, three per day, of which one may exceed 26 inches.
Open year round to hunting; additional regulations are on pamphlet page 6.

notes.item: Southern flounder is closed and unlawful to possess until the Sept. 1 opening. Topsail Sound is coastal water, so Marine Fisheries governs it and not the inland digest.

WVDNR has published its 2026-27 migratory bird regulations, and they came out in July rather than August as this paper had expected. Dove, snipe, rail, goose and duck dates are in that separate publication and not in the hunting summary table, so no migratory date is printed here. HIP registration is required. Deer and bear bag limits are likewise not in the table.

sections.label: On the Water

waters.read: 761 cfs - blown out. Stay on the bank.
waters.working: Down from 4420 cfs a day ago, which is a fast recession, but still several times a normal August flow and nothing here is wadeable. Watch for the number to fall back under about 300 cfs. When it does the seams along the undercut banks clear first, and a heavy stonefly nymph or a sculpin pattern goes in there before anything else.

waters.near: 14 miles above R.C. Byrd Locks and Dam
waters.read: 30.0 ft and rising - up and pushing. Expect colour and current; fish the slack behind anything solid.
waters.working: Up almost two feet on the day and still coloured, so the fish are off the main channel. Shad are the forage: a white swimbait worked through the slack behind the wing dams and in the barge cuts is the first look.

waters.near: below R.C. Byrd Locks and Dam
waters.read: 36.1 ft and rising - high water. Banks are going under and the river is carrying debris.
waters.working: Up five feet in a day and a foot higher than yesterday's reading, so the debris is the hazard rather than the fishing. When it steadies, the lock wall and the riprap hold fish and a crawfish-coloured crankbait tight to the rock is the second look after the swimbait.

waters.reading: Sound highs 1:44 AM and 2:21 PM at Hampstead; lows 7:59 AM and 8:53 PM.
waters.read: Fish the moving water either side of high at 1:44 AM and 2:21 PM in the sound.
waters.working: Tide before lure: the 2:21 p.m. high is the only daylight window and the push into it is the hour that matters. Mud minnows, shrimp and finger mullet are the forage, so a soft plastic or a live bait goes along the grass edges and the oyster bars while the water is moving. Red drum and speckled trout are both open.
waters.note: Hampstead is the sound station and is the read that matters; the oceanfront station at Ocean City Beach pier runs over an hour ahead and is quoted only for a surf read. No water temperature runs today - the Wrightsville Beach gauge returned none for the third morning.

sections.note: USGS does not gauge the Ohio at R.C. Byrd, and the Corps tailwater data is not reachable from this pipeline. The two gauges above are the ones that bracket the dam, and neither is the tailwater.

kicker: The Williams has dropped from 4420 cfs to 761 in a day, and the Ohio is still coming up.
